title: Louis Armstrong at the sessions and "Special Delivery Blues"
summary: She recalls being buddies with Louis, who had a jealous wife, and how he joined "Special Delivery Blues" while her husband Matt was nervous.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, do you remember the session that you did with Louie, Louis Armstrong? Could you -- do you remember those sessions, how they went? How was he? How did he act?

Me and Louie was buddies. We didn't go out together, we never did go out together because Louie had a wife who was a jealous woman, ______, a jealous woman. The only time I'd have fun with Louie was when he'd come rehearsing with my brother. My brother, they would have a rehearsing hour, all the trumpet players and all of them get around there and started playing, rehearsing. And I'd be there playing the piano and everything and Louis would be in the -- and we used to (inaudible).
You used to call him -- you used to talk about he looked like a country boy when he first came to Chicago.
That man that was in the choir ______ kind of like Louie.
(Inaudible) kind of looked like Louie. Kind of looked like Louie.
Uh-huh, good-natured. So I'd say -- so I'd try to get my husband ______ sing this song about "Special Delivery Blues."
And so we was trying to make a good record out of it, a real good record.
It was a real good record.
And so Louie say, "Play 'Special' like the mailman." My husband was scared to death.

Just talking to (unintelligible). Matt was scared -- my husband was named Matt -- Matt was scared to death. Louis say, "Go on now, (inaudible)." So my brother Herschel played the piano and so Herschel was playing Herschel ______ and Louis said, "Special." I said, "Lord, it must have been from --" I said, "It must be from my man." (Unintelligible) and he was (unintelligible). And oh, Louis sure did go to town with that song and I'm telling you the truth.
